items.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 with 20% Price Cut
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, its most capable models for coding, finance, and science. Fable 5.2 is priced at $8/$40 per million tokens — 20% below Fable 5.1 — while delivering output up to 30% faster. Mythos 5.2 is a restricted variant with select safety guardrails removed, available only to vetted organizations for specialized research.
items.whyItMatters: Anthropic's price cut makes frontier AI significantly more accessible to developers, while Mythos 5.2's selective safety removal for vetted organizations opens important questions about how capability and safety are balanced at the frontier.

knowledgeChecks.question: By how much did Anthropic reduce the price of Claude Fable 5.2 compared to Fable 5.1?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Fable 5.2 is priced 20% below Fable 5.1, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, while also being up to 30% faster.

knowledgeChecks.question: What distinguishes Claude Mythos 5.2 from Claude Fable 5.2?
options: Mythos 5.2 is cheaper and faster than Fable 5.2
Mythos 5.2 has a larger context window
Mythos 5.2 has certain safety guardrails removed and is restricted to vetted organizations
Mythos 5.2 is an open-source version of Fable 5.2
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Mythos 5.2 is Fable 5.2 with select safety safeguards removed, restricted to vetted organizations for specialized scientific and research use cases.

items.title: NVIDIA Unveils GR00T 2 World Action Model for Robot Learning at CoRL 2026
items.summary: NVIDIA unveiled GR00T 2 at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2026 in Austin — a 2-billion-parameter 'world action model' that predicts future views and actions to enable robots to learn from human video demonstrations. The system achieves 71% average task success rate from just one demonstration per task. Open-source code is targeted for release in December 2026.
items.whyItMatters: GR00T 2's ability to learn new tasks from a single human demonstration represents a major step toward generalist robots that could be deployed across diverse real-world environments with minimal task-specific training.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the key capability that distinguishes GR00T 2 as a 'world action model'?
options: It runs entirely on-device without cloud connectivity
It predicts future visual states and actions to enable robot task learning
It uses reinforcement learning from human feedback exclusively
It was trained on 100 million robot teleoperation hours
knowledgeChecks.explanation: GR00T 2 is called a 'world action model' because it jointly predicts future visual states (what the world will look like) and the actions needed to reach those states, enabling one-shot learning from human video demonstrations.

knowledgeChecks.question: What average task success rate does GR00T 2 achieve from a single human demonstration?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: NVIDIA reports GR00T 2 achieves 71% average success across tasks when given just one demonstration per task, a significant improvement over previous one-shot robotic learning approaches.

items.title: Meta Releases Muse Ember 1.0: A Lightweight Model Built for Agentic Workflows
items.summary: Meta released Muse Ember 1.0, a lightweight language model optimized for repetitive agentic tasks, priced at just $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. The model features a 1-million-token context window and is designed for developers building high-volume, cost-sensitive AI agent pipelines. An independent benchmark showed it scoring 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
items.whyItMatters: As AI agents move from demos to production, the cost of inference at scale becomes a major bottleneck. Muse Ember gives developers an affordable option for the high-frequency, lower-complexity calls that make up the bulk of agentic workflows.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the input token price for Meta's Muse Ember 1.0?
options: $0.01 per million tokens
$0.10 per million tokens
$1.00 per million tokens
$8.00 per million tokens
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Muse Ember 1.0 is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens, making it one of the most affordable frontier-class models for high-volume agentic applications.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the context window size of Meta's Muse Ember 1.0?
options: 128K tokens
256K tokens
512K tokens
1M tokens
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Muse Ember 1.0 supports a 1-million-token context window, enabling it to handle very long documents and conversation histories within a single inference call.

items.title: Anthropic Begins IPO Roadshow Targeting $1.2–1.3 Trillion Valuation
items.summary: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow on November 9, 2026, targeting a trading debut around November 19–20. The expected valuation has moderated to approximately $1.2–1.3 trillion, down from earlier estimates of up to $1.75 trillion. The company is simultaneously releasing new Claude models during the roadshow, signaling continued product momentum ahead of the public offering.
items.whyItMatters: Anthropic's IPO will serve as a critical market test for how investors value AI safety-focused companies and could set the valuation baseline for other AI lab public offerings.

knowledgeChecks.question: What valuation range is Anthropic targeting for its IPO?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Anthropic's roadshow valuation has converged around $1.2–1.3 trillion, down from earlier estimates of up to $1.75 trillion as market expectations moderated.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is notable about Anthropic releasing new Claude models during its IPO roadshow?
options: It is required by SEC regulations for tech IPOs
It demonstrates continued product momentum to potential investors
It was done to avoid the SEC quiet period restrictions
It signals Anthropic plans to open-source its models after the IPO
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Releasing new models during an IPO roadshow is unusual and signals to investors that the company has strong ongoing product development momentum, which can support a higher valuation.

items.title: Google Launches TPU 8tx with Confidential Computing and TPU 8i Max for AI Training
items.summary: Google announced two new custom AI chips: the TPU 8tx, which pairs its 8t silicon with AMD EPYC hosts to enable confidential computing for sensitive workloads, and the TPU 8i Max, which combines two 8i chips to double compute capacity, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth for large-scale training. The 8tx is designed to process encrypted data throughout the entire AI inference cycle.
items.whyItMatters: Confidential computing in AI hardware could unlock deployments in healthcare, finance, and government sectors where regulatory requirements prevent sensitive data from being processed in unencrypted form.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the primary innovation of Google's TPU 8tx chip?
options: It doubles the number of tensor cores compared to the previous generation
It enables confidential computing by processing sensitive data while keeping it encrypted
It is the first TPU designed for edge deployment without cloud connectivity
It supports multi-modal inputs including video and audio natively
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The TPU 8tx pairs Google's 8t silicon with AMD EPYC hosts to enable confidential computing — processing AI workloads on encrypted data, making it suitable for sensitive enterprise and government use cases.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the TPU 8i Max achieve its increased performance?
options: By using a new 3nm manufacturing process
By adding a dedicated neural network accelerator co-processor
By combining two 8i chips to double compute, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth
By using optical interconnects instead of electrical connections
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The TPU 8i Max achieves higher performance by combining two 8i chips, which Google states doubles the compute capacity, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth compared to a single 8i chip.

items.title: Fireworks AI Discloses Security Breach Exposing Customer Data and AI Model Weights
items.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed that a third-party hosting provider was breached on October 23, allowing attackers to access billing data and, for some accounts, customer datasets and partial AI model weights. The company attributes the attack to 'LLMjacking' — the targeted theft of AI model credentials and assets for resale or competitive espionage. This is the second security incident affecting Fireworks AI this year.
items.whyItMatters: LLMjacking represents an emerging class of cyberattack targeting the growing value of trained AI models and inference infrastructure, signaling that AI assets are now attractive enough to warrant the same security posture as financial data.

knowledgeChecks.question: What term describes the type of cyberattack that targeted Fireworks AI?
options: Prompt injection
Model poisoning
LLMjacking
Adversarial example attack
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Fireworks AI described the attack as 'LLMjacking' — a form of cyberattack that targets AI model weights, credentials, and inference infrastructure rather than traditional data or financial assets.

knowledgeChecks.question: What was the original entry point for the Fireworks AI breach?
options: A phishing attack on a Fireworks employee
A vulnerability in Fireworks AI's API
A breach at a third-party hosting provider
A supply chain attack on an open-source dependency
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The attackers gained access through a third-party hosting provider used by Fireworks AI for R&D machines, highlighting the security risks that arise from dependencies on external infrastructure providers.
